b2-10-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Would Have Happened
b2-10-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you were late to meet him in Budapest. You missed the tram, and you say what would have happened if you had left earlier.
b2-10-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what would have happened if you had left earlier.
cues: Say what you would have done if you had left earlier
b2-10-01.target: Si hubiera salido más temprano, habría llegado a tiempo.
b2-10-01.english: If I had left earlier, I would have arrived on time.
b2-10-01.canDo: I can use si hubiera and habría with a past participle to say what would have happened.

b2-10-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Ways to Say It
b2-10-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague tells you that the time of the meeting changed, and nobody told you. You say what you would have done if you had known.
b2-10-02.prompt: Tell your colleague what you would have done if you had known.
cues: Say that you did not know
Say what you would have done, using hubiera in the result
b2-10-02.target: Si lo hubiera sabido, hubiera llegado más temprano a la reunión.
b2-10-02.english: If I had known, I would have arrived at the meeting earlier.
b2-10-02.canDo: I can use hubiera and a past participle in place of habría in the result clause of a past counterfactual.

b2-10-03.title: Communicative Challenge: I Should Have
b2-10-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you regret anything about a day you had in Budapest. You regret not having left earlier.
b2-10-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you should have done and say that you regret it.
cues: Say what you should have done
b2-10-03.target: Debería haber salido más temprano y me arrepiento de no haberlo hecho.
b2-10-03.english: I should have left earlier, and I regret not having done so.
b2-10-03.canDo: I can say what I or someone else should have done with debería haber and tendría que haber.

b2-10-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Without Si
b2-10-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will come to the meeting on Monday. You are not sure, because of the work you have.
b2-10-04.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do if you had time, without using si.
cues: Give the condition without si, using de
b2-10-04.target: De tener tiempo, iría contigo, pero tengo mucho trabajo.
b2-10-04.english: If I had time, I would go with you, but I have a lot of work.
b2-10-04.canDo: I can say a condition without si with de and an infinitive, in the present and the past.

b2-10-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Even If
b2-10-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos missed the train in Budapest. Carlos says that you should have left earlier. You answer that it would not have mattered.
b2-10-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that even if you had left earlier, you would not have arrived in time.
cues: Say that you would not have arrived in time
b2-10-05.target: Aun cuando hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos llegado a tiempo.
b2-10-05.english: Even if we had left earlier, we would not have arrived on time.
b2-10-05.canDo: I can drop si and begin a past counterfactual with hubiera and a past participle.

b2-10-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Looking Back
b2-10-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you would do anything differently about last week. You say what you would have done and what you regret.
b2-10-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you would have done with more time, and what you regret.
cues: Say what you would have done with more time
b2-10-consolidation.target: Si hubiera tenido más tiempo, habría ayudado más, y me arrepiento de no haberlo hecho.
b2-10-consolidation.english: If I had had more time, I would have helped more, and I regret not having done so.
b2-10-consolidation.canDo: I can say what would have happened with si hubiera and habría or hubiera and a past participle.
